questions.question: Which statement about a Java constructor is true?
options: It has the same name as the class and no return type
It can have any name if marked with new
questions.explanation: A constructor shares the class name and declares no return type at all, not even void.

questions.question: When does the compiler add a default constructor to a class?
options: Only when the class declares no constructor at all
Always, in addition to any constructors you write
Only when the class has a main method
Only when every field is final
questions.explanation: The compiler adds the empty no-parameter constructor only if the class has no constructor of its own.

questions.question: What does this print? class Lamp { int watts; boolean on; } ... Lamp l = new Lamp(); System.out.println(l.watts + " " + l.on);
questions.explanation: The JVM fills fields with defaults before any constructor code runs: 0 for int and false for boolean.

questions.question: class Tent { int size; Tent(int size) { this.size = size; } } ... Tent t = new Tent(); Why does this fail to compile?
options: Writing Tent(int) removed the default no-arg constructor
new cannot be used without arguments
questions.explanation: Once any constructor exists, the compiler stops adding the no-arg one, so new Tent() has nothing to call.

questions.question: Where must a this() or super() call appear inside a constructor?
options: Anywhere, as long as it appears once
questions.explanation: Both calls must be the first statement, which is also why one constructor cannot contain both.

questions.question: What does this print? class Kiosk { Kiosk() { this(3); System.out.print("A"); } Kiosk(int n) { System.out.print("B" + n); } } ... new Kiosk();
questions.explanation: this(3) runs the int constructor first, printing B3, and then the rest of the no-arg body prints A.

questions.question: class Fan { int speed; void Fan() { speed = 3; } } ... new Fan().speed prints 0. Why?
options: speed is reset by the garbage collector
void Fan() is a method, not a constructor, so it never runs on new
The field must be declared after the constructor
questions.explanation: Adding void makes it an ordinary method. The compiler supplies a default constructor, and speed keeps its default 0.

questions.question: In what order does the JVM build an object with new?
options: Memory, field defaults, chained call and initialisers, constructor body
questions.explanation: Memory is reserved, fields get defaults, this() or super() and field initialisers run, and then the body finishes the job.

questions.question: What does this print? class Dock { Dock() { System.out.print("D"); } } class Pier extends Dock { Pier() { System.out.print("P"); } } ... new Pier();
questions.explanation: The compiler inserts super() at the top of Pier(), so the parent constructor prints D before P.

questions.question: Why would a class make all of its constructors private?
options: To stop outside code from calling new, as in a singleton
questions.explanation: Private constructors block direct creation from outside, which is used by singletons, factories and utility classes.
